Chapter Eight: Small Victories and Quiet Progress
Imagine a place where change just... crawls. Where setbacks aren’t rare—they’re part of daily life. In North Korea, progress doesn’t come with fanfare or big headlines. It’s more like a whisper—quiet, sometimes barely visible, but it’s there if you know where to look.
So, what does progress actually look like in a setting like this? Let me share a story. There was a training program launched for local workers—pretty straightforward, right? The idea was to teach new skills, boost efficiency, and maybe, just maybe, help people feel proud of their work again.
At first? Doubt was everywhere. Most folks had never touched modern equipment, and you could see the fear—no one wanted to mess up. But week after week, something changed. Confidence started to grow. There was this young technician—used to keep to himself, always looking down—but as he picked up new skills, he stepped up and became a real leader on the shop floor. Then there was a group of women, who used to be stuck with the dullest jobs. They learned to use a new machine, nailed it, and suddenly, they were trusted with way more responsibility.
These stories? They won’t make the news. But for the people involved, they’re life-changing. For the foreign team helping out, it’s a quiet kind of satisfaction. Sure, the work is tough, and there are plenty of hurdles, but the impact is real. I’ll never forget the day a worker pulled the manager aside, looked him in the eye, and said, “Thank you for believing in us.” Just a few words, but it meant the world.
Of course, not everything goes smoothly. Sometimes a new product launch gets pushed back because the power drops out. Or a shipment of crucial supplies disappears at the border. But every time there’s a problem, the team gets creative. They learn to celebrate the little wins: a training session that goes off without a hitch, a machine that gets fixed, or even just a full day with no interruptions.
And you know what? Progress isn’t just happening at work. Outside, it’s just as subtle. Picture this: a local family, once nervous around foreigners, invites a foreign colleague to a birthday party. Kids who used to stare in wide-eyed curiosity now greet visitors with shy, genuine smiles. Little by little, trust begins to grow.
In North Korea, change doesn’t happen by the mile—it’s more like inch by inch. But if you pay attention, those signs of progress really are everywhere. It’s a powerful reminder: even when things are tough, hope and determination can quietly move mountains.
